Macie can detect PII such as names, email addresses, credit card numbers, and other sensitive data types. It generates findings and alerts when sensitive data is discovered.
wrong_explanation_1: AWS CloudTrail logs API calls to AWS services for auditing purposes. It does not scan S3 objects for sensitive data or detect PII.
wrong_explanation_2: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior. It does not scan S3 objects for sensitive data or detect PII.
wrong_explanation_3: AWS Config tracks configuration changes to AWS resources and evaluates compliance with rules. It does not scan S3 objects for sensitive data or detect PII.

scenario: A data engineering team needs to mask Social Security Numbers (SSNs) in a dataset before sharing it with an external analytics partner. The masked values must be consistent — the same SSN should always produce the same masked value — so that the partner can still perform joins and aggregations. Which technique should be used?
correct_answer: Tokenization (deterministic encryption or format-preserving encryption)
wrong_answer_1: Random masking (replace SSN with random digits)
wrong_answer_2: Nullification (replace SSN with NULL)
wrong_answer_3: Truncation (keep only the last 4 digits of the SSN)
correct_explanation: Tokenization replaces sensitive values with consistent tokens using deterministic encryption or format-preserving encryption. The same SSN always maps to the same token, preserving referential integrity for joins and aggregations while protecting the actual SSN value from the external partner.
wrong_explanation_1: Random masking replaces SSNs with random values, which are different each time. This breaks referential integrity — the same SSN would produce different masked values, making joins and aggregations across datasets impossible.
wrong_explanation_2: Nullification replaces SSNs with NULL, which completely removes the value. The partner cannot perform joins or aggregations on NULL values, making this approach unsuitable when consistent masked values are required.
wrong_explanation_3: Truncation to the last 4 digits reduces uniqueness significantly — many customers may share the same last 4 digits. This approach does not provide sufficient de-identification and would produce incorrect join results.

scenario: You operate a media streaming service whose users are distributed across six continents. End users have complained about slow video startup times when accessing content stored in a single S3 bucket in us-east-1. Which AWS infrastructure component is designed to address this latency problem by caching content close to end users?
correct_answer: Edge locations
wrong_answer_1: Availability Zones
wrong_answer_2: AWS Regions
wrong_answer_3: AWS Local Zones
correct_explanation: Edge locations are part of the Amazon CloudFront global network. They cache static and dynamic content close to viewers worldwide, reducing the latency users experience when retrieving large objects like video segments. There are far more edge locations than Regions, so users almost always connect to a nearby cache.
wrong_explanation_1: Availability Zones are isolated data centers within a single Region. They provide intra-Region high availability but do not bring content closer to globally distributed users.
wrong_explanation_2: Adding more Regions could reduce latency but is operationally heavy and typically reserved for compliance or major workload distribution — not low-latency content delivery, which is what edge locations are purpose-built for.
wrong_explanation_3: Local Zones place compute and storage close to a specific metropolitan area for ultra-low-latency applications. They are not designed as a global content cache like edge locations are.

scenario: An ML team wants to find the optimal hyperparameters for a SageMaker training job without manually running dozens of experiments. They want to minimize validation loss while staying within a budget of 20 training jobs. Which SageMaker feature should they use?
correct_answer: SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning (Hyperparameter Optimization)
wrong_answer_1: SageMaker Autopilot
wrong_answer_2: SageMaker Experiments
wrong_answer_3: SageMaker Debugger
correct_explanation: Amazon SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning (also called Hyperparameter Optimization or HPO) automates the search for optimal hyperparameters. It supports Bayesian optimization, random search, and Hyperband strategies, and can run up to a specified maximum number of training jobs — making it ideal for finding the best hyperparameters within a 20-job budget.
wrong_explanation_1: SageMaker Autopilot automates the entire ML pipeline including algorithm selection, feature engineering, and hyperparameter tuning for tabular datasets. It is not designed for tuning a specific user-defined model architecture with custom hyperparameter ranges.
wrong_explanation_2: SageMaker Experiments is a tracking and organization tool for logging metrics, parameters, and artifacts across training runs. It does not automate the search for optimal hyperparameters — it only records the results of experiments that are run manually.
wrong_explanation_3: SageMaker Debugger monitors training jobs for issues like vanishing gradients, overfitting, and resource utilization. It does not perform hyperparameter search or optimization.

scenario: A regulated organization needs the API call audit trail for Amazon Bedrock — every InvokeModel, CreateAgent, CreateKnowledgeBase, etc. — over the past year. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this audit history?
correct_answer: AWS CloudTrail
wrong_answer_1: Amazon CloudWatch metrics
wrong_answer_2: AWS Trusted Advisor
wrong_answer_3: AWS Config rules
correct_explanation: AWS CloudTrail records every AWS API call including Bedrock operations. CloudTrail Lake retains and queries event data for compliance investigations over long periods.
wrong_explanation_1: CloudWatch metrics show numerical telemetry over time, not per-call audit history.
wrong_explanation_2: Trusted Advisor produces recommendations, not API audit logs.
wrong_explanation_3: Config rules evaluate resource configurations; they are not the API audit trail.

scenario: A company is building a mobile application that allows users to upload photos directly to Amazon S3. The backend uses Amazon Cognito for user authentication. The solutions architect needs to ensure that each authenticated user can only upload to their own folder in S3 (e.g., s3://bucket/users/{cognito-user-id}/) and cannot read or write to other users' folders. Which approach should the architect use?
correct_answer: Create an IAM role for the Cognito identity pool with a policy that uses the ${cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub} condition variable to scope S3 access to the authenticated user's folder.
wrong_answer_1: Create a separate S3 bucket for each user and assign each user an IAM role with access to their own bucket.
wrong_answer_2: Use S3 bucket ACLs to grant each user read/write access to their own folder prefix.
wrong_answer_3: Create a Lambda function that validates the user's Cognito token and proxies all S3 upload requests, enforcing folder-level access control.
correct_explanation: Amazon Cognito identity pools issue temporary AWS credentials via IAM roles. IAM policy variables allow the policy to dynamically reference the authenticated user's Cognito identity ID using ${cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub}. This scopes the S3 permissions to the user's specific folder prefix at the IAM policy level, without requiring separate buckets or custom proxy logic.
wrong_explanation_1: Creating a separate S3 bucket per user is operationally unscalable — AWS accounts have soft limits on bucket counts and managing thousands of buckets adds significant overhead. IAM policy variables achieve the same isolation within a single bucket.
wrong_explanation_2: S3 bucket ACLs are a legacy access control mechanism that operates at the object level and does not support IAM identity-based conditions or folder-level scoping per authenticated user. ACLs cannot reference Cognito identity IDs.
wrong_explanation_3: A Lambda proxy adds latency, cost, and operational complexity for every upload. It also requires the Lambda function to have broad S3 permissions, which is a wider blast radius than the scoped IAM role approach. IAM policy variables solve this natively without a proxy.

scenario: A developer is building an application that stores user passwords in Amazon DynamoDB. The developer wants to ensure that passwords cannot be recovered even if the DynamoDB table is compromised. Which approach should the developer implement?
correct_answer: Hash the passwords using a strong one-way hashing algorithm with a unique salt per user (such as bcrypt) before storing them in DynamoDB.
wrong_answer_1: Encrypt the passwords using AES-256 with a KMS customer managed key before storing them in DynamoDB.
wrong_answer_2: Store the passwords in a DynamoDB table encrypted with SSE-KMS to protect them at rest.
wrong_answer_3: Base64-encode the passwords before storing them in DynamoDB.
correct_explanation: Passwords should never be stored in a recoverable form. One-way hashing with a salt (using algorithms like bcrypt, Argon2, or scrypt) produces a hash that cannot be reversed to obtain the original password. During authentication, the submitted password is hashed and compared to the stored hash. Even if the database is compromised, the original passwords cannot be recovered.
wrong_explanation_1: Encrypting passwords with AES-256 and KMS is reversible — anyone with access to the KMS key can decrypt and recover the original passwords. Encryption protects data in transit and at rest but does not prevent recovery of the original value. Passwords must be hashed, not encrypted.
wrong_explanation_2: DynamoDB SSE-KMS encrypts the table data at rest, protecting against unauthorized access to the underlying storage. However, the passwords are still stored in their original form within the encrypted table. Anyone with DynamoDB read permissions can retrieve the plaintext passwords.
wrong_explanation_3: Base64 encoding is a reversible encoding scheme, not encryption or hashing. It provides no security whatsoever — any attacker can trivially decode a base64-encoded password. This is not an acceptable approach for storing passwords.

scenario: A company has years of on-premises backups stored on tape and wants to retain them in AWS for long-term archival, presented as a virtual tape library to the existing backup software. Which AWS service is the appropriate choice?
correct_answer: AWS Storage Gateway (Tape Gateway)
wrong_answer_1: AWS Snowmobile
wrong_answer_2: AWS Direct Connect
wrong_answer_3: Amazon EBS
correct_explanation: AWS Storage Gateway's Tape Gateway presents AWS-backed storage as a virtual tape library (iSCSI VTL). On-premises backup software writes to virtual tapes that are stored in S3 and Glacier, replacing physical tape infrastructure.
wrong_explanation_1: Snowmobile is a now-rare exabyte-scale data transfer service in a tractor-trailer truck. It is not the right fit for ongoing virtual-tape-library replacement.
wrong_explanation_2: Direct Connect is a private network connection, not a tape library.
wrong_explanation_3: EBS is block storage attached to EC2 instances, not a virtual tape library presented to backup software.

scenario: A team needs to provision and automatically renew public TLS/SSL certificates for use with Amazon CloudFront and Application Load Balancers. Which AWS service should they use?
correct_answer: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
wrong_answer_1: AWS Secrets Manager
wrong_answer_2: AWS Key Management Service
wrong_answer_3: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
correct_explanation: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provisions, manages, and automatically renews TLS/SSL certificates. ACM integrates natively with CloudFront, Application Load Balancers, and other AWS services, removing the burden of manual certificate renewal.
wrong_explanation_1: Secrets Manager handles credential storage and rotation, not TLS certificates.
wrong_explanation_2: KMS manages cryptographic keys used for data encryption — not TLS certificates.
wrong_explanation_3: Parameter Store stores configuration values and secrets but does not issue or renew TLS certificates.

scenario: A remote scientific field team needs to collect terabytes of data from sensors at a location with no reliable internet connection and later ship that data physically to AWS. Which Snow Family device is the BEST fit for this small-scale field collection?
correct_answer: AWS Snowcone
wrong_answer_1: AWS Snowmobile
wrong_answer_2: AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized
wrong_answer_3: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration
correct_explanation: AWS Snowcone is the smallest Snow Family device — portable, rugged, and battery-powered — designed for small-scale data collection and edge compute in remote, often disconnected environments.
wrong_explanation_1: Snowmobile is an exabyte-scale truck-based transfer for massive datacenter-scale migrations, not portable field collection.
wrong_explanation_2: Snowball Edge Compute Optimized is larger and intended for heavier edge-compute workloads. Snowcone is the smaller field-portable choice.
wrong_explanation_3: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads to S3 — it requires an internet connection, which the scenario explicitly lacks.

scenario: Your API Gateway REST API uses a Lambda Authorizer to validate custom JWT tokens issued by an internal identity provider. The authorizer is being invoked on every request, adding 200ms of latency. The tokens are valid for 1 hour. How can the latency be reduced without changing the authorization logic?
correct_answer: Enable the Lambda Authorizer cache in API Gateway with a TTL matching the token validity period (up to 3600 seconds).
wrong_answer_1: Switch from a Lambda Authorizer to a Cognito User Pool Authorizer, which has built-in caching.
wrong_answer_2: Increase the Lambda Authorizer function's memory to reduce its execution time.
wrong_answer_3: Enable API Gateway response caching on the stage to cache the full API response including authorization.
correct_explanation: API Gateway Lambda Authorizers support a result cache with a configurable TTL (up to 3600 seconds). When caching is enabled, the authorization result for a given token is cached and reused for subsequent requests with the same token, eliminating the Lambda invocation for cached tokens. Setting the TTL to match the token validity period (3600 seconds) means the authorizer is only invoked once per token per hour.
wrong_explanation_1: Switching to a Cognito User Pool Authorizer would require the internal identity provider to issue Cognito-compatible JWT tokens, which may not be possible without significant changes to the identity infrastructure. The question asks for a solution that does not change the authorization logic.
wrong_explanation_2: Increasing Lambda memory reduces execution time for compute-bound operations. A Lambda Authorizer that validates a JWT token is primarily doing cryptographic verification and is already fast. The 200ms latency is the per-invocation overhead of invoking Lambda on every request — caching eliminates the invocation entirely.
wrong_explanation_3: API Gateway response caching caches the full API response (status code, headers, body) for a given request. It does not cache authorization results. A cached response bypasses the integration entirely, which is different from caching the authorization decision while still executing the integration.

scenario: An ML team is preparing a dataset for a deep learning model that processes tabular data. The dataset contains 200 features, many of which are highly correlated. The team wants to reduce dimensionality to remove redundant features and speed up training while retaining the most important variance in the data. Which technique should be applied?
correct_answer: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
wrong_answer_1: SMOTE oversampling
wrong_answer_2: Target encoding
wrong_answer_3: Min-max normalization
correct_explanation: PCA is a dimensionality reduction technique that transforms correlated features into a smaller set of uncorrelated principal components that capture the most variance in the data. Reducing 200 correlated features to a smaller set of principal components removes redundancy, speeds up training, and can improve model generalization.
wrong_explanation_1: SMOTE is an oversampling technique for addressing class imbalance. It generates synthetic minority class samples and does not reduce feature dimensionality or address correlated features.
wrong_explanation_2: Target encoding is a categorical feature encoding technique. It does not reduce the number of features or address multicollinearity among numeric features.
wrong_explanation_3: Min-max normalization scales feature values to a [0,1] range. It does not reduce dimensionality or remove redundant correlated features.

scenario: Which of the following is a foundation model provider whose models are available through Amazon Bedrock?
correct_answer: Anthropic (Claude)
wrong_answer_1: OpenAI (ChatGPT)
wrong_answer_2: Google (Gemini)
wrong_answer_3: Microsoft (Phi)
correct_explanation: Anthropic's Claude family is available through Amazon Bedrock. Bedrock also hosts foundation models from Amazon (Titan, Nova), Meta (Llama), Cohere, AI21 Labs, Mistral, Stability AI, and others — but not OpenAI, Google, or Microsoft directly.
wrong_explanation_1: OpenAI models are accessed through OpenAI's own API and Microsoft Azure, not through Amazon Bedrock.
wrong_explanation_2: Google's Gemini models are available through Google's services, not Bedrock.
wrong_explanation_3: Microsoft's Phi models are not part of the Bedrock model catalog.

scenario: A company is running a large-scale data processing job on Amazon EMR that takes 6 hours to complete. The job runs once per week and is fault-tolerant with checkpointing enabled. The company wants to minimize the cost of running the EMR cluster. Which combination of instance purchasing options should the solutions architect recommend?
correct_answer: Use On-Demand Instances for the EMR master node and core nodes, and Spot Instances for task nodes to reduce compute costs while maintaining cluster stability.
wrong_answer_1: Use Spot Instances for all nodes including the master node to maximize cost savings.
wrong_answer_2: Use Reserved Instances for all EMR nodes with a 1-year term to get a discount on the weekly job.
wrong_answer_3: Use On-Demand Instances for all nodes to ensure the job completes without interruption.
correct_explanation: In EMR, the master node coordinates the cluster and the core nodes store HDFS data — losing either causes the cluster to fail. Task nodes only process data and do not store HDFS data, so they can be safely replaced if interrupted. Using Spot for task nodes provides significant cost savings while On-Demand master and core nodes ensure cluster stability.
wrong_explanation_1: Using Spot Instances for the master node is risky — if the master node is interrupted, the entire EMR cluster terminates and the job fails. Even with checkpointing, restarting the cluster and job from a checkpoint adds significant time and cost.
wrong_explanation_2: Reserved Instances provide discounts for continuous usage. A job that runs only once per week uses the reserved capacity for approximately 6 out of 168 hours (3.6% utilization). The reservation cost for the unused 96.4% of the time makes this far more expensive than On-Demand pricing.
wrong_explanation_3: Using On-Demand for all nodes is the safest option but not the most cost-effective. Since task nodes can be safely replaced with Spot Instances without risking cluster stability, using On-Demand for all nodes misses a significant cost optimization opportunity.

scenario: An ML team needs to present a structured document describing a model's intended use, training data, performance, limitations, and risks for governance review. Which Amazon SageMaker feature is purpose-built for this?
correct_answer: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards
wrong_answer_1: Amazon SageMaker Model Dashboard
wrong_answer_2: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
wrong_answer_3: Amazon SageMaker Studio Lab
correct_explanation: SageMaker Model Cards capture critical model documentation — intended use, training data, evaluation metrics, ethical considerations, risks, and limitations — in a structured format suited for governance and compliance reviews.
wrong_explanation_1: Model Dashboard provides operational status of running models; it is not the structured governance document the scenario describes.
wrong_explanation_2: JumpStart is the model hub for browsing and deploying models, not a governance document.
wrong_explanation_3: Studio Lab is a free Jupyter notebook environment, not a documentation feature.

scenario: A company is deploying an application to Elastic Beanstalk. After each deployment, the application needs to register itself with an internal service discovery system by calling an external API. This registration must happen after the application server starts and before the instance is added back to the load balancer. Which Elastic Beanstalk hook is appropriate for this post-deployment registration step?
correct_answer: Use a container_commands: directive in .ebextensions with the registration script, which runs after the application is deployed but before the web server starts serving traffic.
wrong_answer_1: Use a commands: directive in .ebextensions to run the registration script before the application source is extracted.
wrong_answer_2: Add the registration script to the EC2 instance's user data so it runs when the instance first launches.
wrong_answer_3: Use an AWS Lambda function triggered by an Elastic Beanstalk SNS event notification to call the registration API after deployment.
correct_explanation: container_commands in .ebextensions execute after the application source bundle is extracted and the application is staged, but before the web server is restarted to serve traffic. This is the correct hook for post-deployment tasks that must complete before the instance receives traffic, such as service registration.
wrong_explanation_1: The commands: directive runs before the application source is extracted — before the new application version is in place. Running a registration script at this point would register the instance before the new code is deployed, which is the wrong order for the described requirement.
wrong_explanation_2: EC2 user data runs only once at instance launch, not on subsequent application deployments to existing instances. If Elastic Beanstalk deploys a new application version to a running instance, user data does not re-execute. It cannot serve as a deployment lifecycle hook.
wrong_explanation_3: Elastic Beanstalk SNS event notifications report environment state changes (e.g., environment health changes) but do not provide fine-grained deployment lifecycle hooks. A Lambda function triggered by these events cannot reliably execute at the precise moment between deployment completion and traffic resumption.

scenario: A company has deployed a SageMaker endpoint for a product recommendation model. After several months in production, the team observes that model accuracy has declined. They suspect that the relationship between input features and the target variable has changed over time (concept drift). Which SageMaker Model Monitor monitor type is designed to detect this?
correct_answer: Model quality monitoring
wrong_answer_1: Data quality monitoring
wrong_answer_2: Feature attribution drift monitoring
wrong_answer_3: Bias drift monitoring
correct_explanation: Model quality monitoring compares model predictions against ground truth labels over time to detect degradation in prediction accuracy — which is the direct signal of concept drift (the relationship between features and the target has changed). When ground truth labels are available, model quality monitoring quantifies the actual performance decline.
wrong_explanation_1: Data quality monitoring detects changes in the statistical distribution of input features (data drift). While data drift can cause concept drift, data quality monitoring does not directly measure whether the model's predictions are becoming less accurate.
wrong_explanation_2: Feature attribution drift monitoring tracks changes in SHAP-based feature importance over time. It can indicate that the model is relying on different features, but it does not directly measure prediction accuracy degradation.
wrong_explanation_3: Bias drift monitoring tracks changes in fairness metrics across demographic groups. It does not measure overall model accuracy degradation caused by concept drift.

scenario: Which international standard specifically addresses MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS for AI — analogous to how ISO 9001 addresses quality management or ISO 27001 addresses information security?
correct_answer: ISO/IEC 42001
wrong_answer_1: ISO 9001
wrong_answer_3: PCI-DSS
correct_explanation: ISO/IEC 42001 is the international standard for AI management systems. It provides organizations a framework for governing the AI lifecycle responsibly. AWS supports customers in aligning AI usage with ISO/IEC 42001.
wrong_explanation_1: ISO 9001 addresses quality management systems generally, not AI specifically.
wrong_explanation_2: ISO 27001 addresses information security management, not AI management.
wrong_explanation_3: PCI-DSS addresses payment card data security, unrelated to AI management systems.

scenario: A team notices that their LLM confidently generates factual-sounding statements that are actually incorrect — citing fake papers or attributing quotes to people who never said them. What is this phenomenon commonly called?
correct_answer: Hallucination
wrong_answer_1: Drift
wrong_answer_2: Overfitting
wrong_answer_3: Quantization
correct_explanation: Hallucination is the term for an LLM producing confident, fluent output that is factually wrong or fabricated. Hallucinations are a fundamental limitation of generative LLMs and are often mitigated with RAG, guardrails, or constrained decoding.
wrong_explanation_1: Drift refers to changes in data or model behavior over time, not to fabricated factual content.
wrong_explanation_2: Overfitting is an ML training problem where a model memorizes training data; it differs from confidently fabricated content during inference.
wrong_explanation_3: Quantization reduces numerical precision of a model's weights to save memory; it is unrelated.

scenario: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of a large language model (LLM)?
correct_answer: A neural network with a very large number of parameters trained to predict the next token in a sequence of text
wrong_answer_1: A linear regression model fit on text data
wrong_answer_2: A database engine optimized for storing language documents
wrong_answer_3: A rule-based system that performs grammar correction only
correct_explanation: LLMs are large transformer-based neural networks with billions of parameters trained — at scale — to predict the next token (and related self-supervised objectives) over enormous text corpora. This is what gives them their general language abilities.
wrong_explanation_1: Linear regression cannot model language at the scale and complexity LLMs do.
wrong_explanation_2: LLMs are not databases.
wrong_explanation_3: Rule-based grammar tools are narrow, hand-engineered systems — not LLMs.

scenario: Which model explainability technique fits a simple, interpretable model LOCALLY around each prediction to estimate feature contributions for that single prediction?
correct_answer: LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations)
wrong_answer_1: K-means clustering
wrong_answer_2: Tokenization
wrong_answer_3: Hyperparameter tuning
correct_explanation: LIME fits a simple, interpretable model (often linear) locally around an individual prediction to estimate which features contributed to that specific outcome. It is a popular model-agnostic explainability tool.
wrong_explanation_1: K-means is an unsupervised clustering algorithm, not an explainability technique.
wrong_explanation_2: Tokenization is text preprocessing.
wrong_explanation_3: Hyperparameter tuning is an optimization activity, not an explainability technique.

scenario: A machine learning engineer is training an XGBoost model on Amazon SageMaker. The training loss decreases steadily but the validation loss starts increasing after epoch 15. What is the most likely cause of this behavior, and what is the recommended remedy?
correct_answer: The model is overfitting; apply early stopping based on the validation metric
wrong_answer_1: The model is underfitting; increase the number of estimators and tree depth
wrong_answer_2: The learning rate is too high; switch to a larger instance type
wrong_answer_3: The training data is too small; collect more training samples before continuing
correct_explanation: When training loss decreases while validation loss increases, the model is overfitting — it is memorizing the training data rather than generalizing. Early stopping monitors the validation metric and halts training when it stops improving, preventing the model from overfitting further. SageMaker supports early stopping natively for XGBoost via the `early_stopping_rounds` hyperparameter.
wrong_explanation_1: Increasing estimators and tree depth would make the model more complex, which would worsen overfitting. Underfitting is characterized by high training loss and high validation loss simultaneously — not by diverging training and validation losses.
wrong_explanation_2: A high learning rate can cause training instability, but it does not explain the specific pattern of decreasing training loss with increasing validation loss. Switching to a larger instance type addresses compute capacity, not overfitting.
wrong_explanation_3: While more data can help with overfitting, the immediate and most direct remedy is early stopping, which can be applied without collecting additional data. Collecting more data is a longer-term strategy and may not be feasible.

scenario: A company is building an order processing system where multiple downstream services (inventory, billing, and shipping) each need to independently process every new order event. The company wants to ensure that a failure in one downstream service does not affect the others and that each service can process events at its own pace. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?
correct_answer: Publish order events to an Amazon SNS topic and have each downstream service subscribe via its own Amazon SQS queue (fan-out pattern).
wrong_answer_1: Publish order events to a single Amazon SQS queue and have all three downstream services poll the same queue.
wrong_answer_2: Write order events directly to each downstream service's database table using Amazon RDS multi-table inserts.
wrong_answer_3: Use Amazon EventBridge to route all order events to a single Lambda function that calls each downstream service synchronously.
correct_explanation: The SNS-to-SQS fan-out pattern decouples producers from consumers. Each downstream service has its own SQS queue subscribed to the SNS topic, so every service receives every event independently. If one service's queue backs up or the service fails, it does not affect the other queues. Each service processes at its own pace using its own queue.
wrong_explanation_1: A single SQS queue means each message is delivered to only one consumer. If all three services poll the same queue, each order event would be processed by only one of the three services, not all three. This does not satisfy the requirement for independent processing by each service.
wrong_explanation_2: Writing directly to each service's database creates tight coupling between the order system and the downstream services. A failure or schema change in any downstream database would directly impact the order processing system, violating the loose coupling requirement.
wrong_explanation_3: Calling each downstream service synchronously from a single Lambda function creates tight coupling and a single point of failure. If any downstream service is slow or unavailable, the Lambda function blocks and the entire processing chain is affected.

scenario: A business analyst wants to build ML models on tabular data using a NO-CODE, drag-and-drop interface inside SageMaker. Which service is purpose-built for this audience?
correct_answer: Amazon SageMaker Canvas
wrong_answer_1: Amazon SageMaker Studio (full IDE)
wrong_answer_2: AWS DeepLens
wrong_answer_3: AWS Cloud9
correct_explanation: Amazon SageMaker Canvas provides a no-code, visual interface for building, training, and using ML models on tabular data. It is targeted at business analysts who want ML capability without writing code.
wrong_explanation_1: SageMaker Studio is the full code-driven IDE for data scientists, not a no-code experience.
wrong_explanation_2: DeepLens (now discontinued) was a deep-learning enabled camera; it is not a no-code tabular ML builder.
wrong_explanation_3: Cloud9 is a code IDE, not a no-code ML builder.

scenario: Which responsible AI dimension is concerned with preventing physical, psychological, or societal harm from an AI system's deployment?
correct_answer: Safety
wrong_answer_1: Explainability
wrong_answer_2: Latency
wrong_answer_3: Cost optimization
correct_explanation: Safety is the responsible AI dimension concerned with avoiding physical, psychological, or societal harm — including misuse, unsafe automation, and unintended consequences. It is essential to responsible deployment of any AI system.
wrong_explanation_1: Explainability focuses on understanding model outputs, not on preventing harm.
wrong_explanation_2: Latency is operational performance.
wrong_explanation_3: Cost optimization is an economic concern, not a safety dimension.

scenario: A data engineering team runs AWS Glue ETL jobs that occasionally fail due to data quality issues or schema changes. The team wants to receive an email notification whenever a Glue job fails so they can investigate and resolve the issue quickly. Which approach provides email notifications for Glue job failures?
correct_answer: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that detects Glue job failure events and sends notifications to an SNS topic
wrong_answer_1: Enable AWS Glue job metrics in CloudWatch and create a CloudWatch alarm
wrong_answer_2: Configure AWS Glue to write job logs to CloudWatch Logs and create a log metric filter
wrong_answer_3: Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate the Glue job and send SNS notifications on failure
correct_explanation: Amazon EventBridge can detect AWS Glue job state change events, including failures. You can create a rule that matches job failure events and routes them to an SNS topic, which sends email notifications to subscribers. This is the native, event-driven approach for monitoring Glue job failures.
wrong_explanation_1: AWS Glue job metrics in CloudWatch track job execution statistics like duration and data processed, but they do not directly indicate job success or failure. CloudWatch alarms on metrics are not the most direct way to detect job failures compared to EventBridge state change events.
wrong_explanation_2: While you can create log metric filters to detect failure patterns in CloudWatch Logs, this requires parsing log messages and is more complex than using EventBridge to detect native Glue job state change events.
wrong_explanation_3: Using Step Functions to orchestrate the Glue job and send SNS notifications on failure works, but it adds unnecessary complexity for a simple notification requirement. EventBridge can detect Glue job failures directly without requiring Step Functions orchestration.

scenario: A retailer's storefront receives heavy traffic on Black Friday and Cyber Monday but only modest traffic the rest of the year. Which AWS Cloud economic benefit allows the company to handle holiday spikes without paying for that peak capacity year-round?
correct_answer: Elasticity
wrong_answer_1: Durability
wrong_answer_2: Loose coupling
wrong_answer_3: Fault tolerance
correct_explanation: Elasticity is the ability to add capacity when demand grows and remove it when demand falls. Pairing elasticity with pay-as-you-go pricing means the retailer pays for peak capacity only during peak periods, dramatically lowering year-round cost compared to provisioning for peak in advance.
wrong_explanation_1: Durability describes the resilience of stored data against loss (e.g., S3's 11 nines of durability). It is unrelated to scaling compute capacity with demand.
wrong_explanation_2: Loose coupling is a design principle that reduces dependencies between components. It enables scalability but does not by itself describe the cost benefit of scaling on demand.
wrong_explanation_3: Fault tolerance is the ability to continue operating despite component failures. It is about availability, not about scaling capacity with demand.

scenario: A company is deploying a new application on AWS and wants to ensure that all API calls made to AWS services from the application are logged for compliance purposes. The security team also wants to receive alerts when specific high-risk API calls are made, such as deleting S3 buckets or modifying security groups. Which combination of services should the solutions architect use?
correct_answer: Enable AWS CloudTrail to log all API calls, then create Amazon CloudWatch Logs metric filters on the CloudTrail log group and configure CloudWatch Alarms to notify an SNS topic for high-risk events.
wrong_answer_1: Enable Amazon GuardDuty and configure findings to trigger SNS notifications for high-risk API calls.
wrong_answer_2: Enable AWS Config to record resource configuration changes and set up Config rules to alert on non-compliant changes.
wrong_answer_3: Enable VPC Flow Logs and use Amazon Athena to query for high-risk API calls.
correct_explanation: AWS CloudTrail records all API calls made in an AWS account. By delivering CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs, you can create metric filters that match specific API call patterns (e.g., DeleteBucket, AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress) and trigger CloudWatch Alarms that notify an SNS topic. This combination satisfies both the logging and alerting requirements.
wrong_explanation_1: Amazon GuardDuty uses CloudTrail events as one of its data sources but focuses on detecting threats and anomalies using ML models. It does not provide granular alerting on specific API calls like DeleteBucket or security group modifications.
wrong_explanation_2: AWS Config records resource configuration states and evaluates them against rules, but it does not capture all API calls. It is focused on configuration compliance, not comprehensive API activity logging and real-time alerting.
wrong_explanation_3: VPC Flow Logs capture network traffic metadata (IP addresses, ports, bytes) at the VPC level. They do not record AWS API calls and cannot be used to detect actions like deleting S3 buckets or modifying security groups.

scenario: A company's application uses Amazon Cognito User Pools for authentication. After a user signs in, the application calls a protected API Gateway endpoint. The API must verify that the caller is an authenticated Cognito user and reject unauthenticated requests with a 401 response. Which API Gateway configuration achieves this with the least custom code?
correct_answer: Create a Cognito User Pool Authorizer in API Gateway and attach it to the protected methods. API Gateway validates the JWT token from the Authorization header against the User Pool automatically.
wrong_answer_1: Create a Lambda Authorizer that decodes the JWT token and calls the Cognito User Pool to verify it on each request.
wrong_answer_2: Enable IAM authorization on the API Gateway methods and use Cognito Identity Pool credentials to sign requests with SigV4.
wrong_answer_3: Use API Gateway resource policies to restrict access to the Cognito User Pool's IP address range.
correct_explanation: The native Cognito User Pool Authorizer validates the JWT token from the Authorization header against the specified User Pool without any custom code. It handles token signature verification, expiry checking, and claim extraction automatically. Unauthenticated requests or requests with invalid tokens receive a 401 Unauthorized response.
wrong_explanation_1: A Lambda Authorizer can validate Cognito tokens but requires writing and maintaining custom JWT validation code, adds per-request Lambda invocation latency, and incurs additional Lambda costs. The native Cognito Authorizer handles this more efficiently with no custom code.
wrong_explanation_2: IAM authorization requires clients to sign requests with SigV4 using AWS credentials obtained from a Cognito Identity Pool. This adds complexity for web and mobile clients and is more appropriate for service-to-service API access, not for end-user authentication with User Pool tokens.
wrong_explanation_3: API Gateway resource policies restrict access based on AWS account, VPC, or IP address — not based on Cognito User Pool identity. Cognito User Pools do not have a fixed IP address range, and this approach would not validate user authentication.

scenario: A help center has English-language content and wants to automatically translate it into French, Spanish, German, and Japanese for international users. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
correct_answer: Amazon Translate
wrong_answer_1: Amazon Comprehend
wrong_answer_2: Amazon Polly
wrong_answer_3: Amazon Lex
correct_explanation: Amazon Translate is the AWS managed neural machine translation service. It supports many language pairs and can translate documents and snippets at scale.
wrong_explanation_1: Comprehend analyzes text for entities and sentiment but does not translate between languages.
wrong_explanation_2: Polly converts text to speech; it does not translate text.
wrong_explanation_3: Lex builds conversational chatbots; it is not a translation service.

scenario: A data engineer is building an ETL pipeline using AWS Glue to process semi-structured JSON data stored in Amazon S3. Some records have inconsistent schemas — fields are missing in some records and additional fields appear in others. The engineer needs to handle schema evolution gracefully without failing the job. Which AWS Glue feature supports this?
correct_answer: AWS Glue DynamicFrame with resolveChoice and schema merging
wrong_answer_1: AWS Glue DataFrame with a strict schema definition
wrong_answer_2: AWS Glue Data Quality rules to reject non-conforming records
wrong_answer_3: Amazon Athena schema-on-read with OPENCSV SerDe
correct_explanation: AWS Glue DynamicFrames are designed for semi-structured data with inconsistent schemas. They support schema merging (combining fields from all records into a unified schema) and resolveChoice (handling fields with multiple data types), allowing the ETL job to process records with varying schemas without failing.
wrong_explanation_1: A Spark DataFrame with a strict schema definition will fail or drop records that do not conform to the defined schema. It does not gracefully handle missing fields or additional fields across records.
wrong_explanation_2: AWS Glue Data Quality rules validate data against constraints and can flag or reject non-conforming records, but they do not resolve schema inconsistencies or allow the job to continue processing records with varying schemas.
wrong_explanation_3: Amazon Athena with schema-on-read applies a schema at query time for CSV data. It is a query service, not an ETL transformation tool, and does not address schema evolution within a Glue ETL pipeline.

scenario: A data scientist discovers that 8% of rows in a training dataset have missing values in a key numeric feature. The feature has a roughly normal distribution and the missingness appears to be random. Which imputation strategy is most appropriate to preserve the statistical properties of the feature?
correct_answer: Impute missing values with the mean of the feature
wrong_answer_1: Drop all rows with missing values
wrong_answer_2: Impute missing values with zero
wrong_answer_3: Impute missing values with the maximum value of the feature
correct_explanation: When data is missing at random and the feature is normally distributed, mean imputation preserves the central tendency of the distribution and introduces minimal bias. It is a standard, statistically sound approach for handling random missingness in numeric features.
wrong_explanation_1: Dropping rows with missing values removes 8% of the training data, which reduces the dataset size and can introduce bias if the missingness is not completely random. This is generally not preferred when imputation is feasible.
wrong_explanation_2: Imputing with zero is only appropriate when zero has a meaningful interpretation in the context of the feature (e.g., no purchases). For a normally distributed feature, replacing missing values with zero would distort the distribution and introduce significant bias.
wrong_explanation_3: Imputing with the maximum value would severely skew the distribution toward the upper end, introducing systematic bias and potentially causing the model to learn incorrect patterns from the imputed values.

scenario: A company runs a content management system where authors publish articles that trigger downstream workflows including image resizing, search indexing, and social media posting. Each workflow is independent and managed by a separate team. The company wants to add new downstream workflows in the future without modifying the publishing service. Which architecture supports this extensibility requirement?
correct_answer: Publish article events to an Amazon SNS topic. Each downstream workflow subscribes to the topic via its own SQS queue. New workflows can be added by creating a new SQS queue and subscribing it to the topic.
wrong_answer_1: Have the publishing service directly invoke each downstream workflow's Lambda function using the AWS SDK.
wrong_answer_2: Write article events to a shared DynamoDB table that each downstream workflow polls for new entries.
wrong_answer_3: Use Amazon EventBridge with a single rule that routes all article events to a Lambda function that calls each downstream workflow in sequence.
correct_explanation: SNS fan-out with SQS subscriptions provides a loosely coupled, extensible architecture. The publishing service only knows about the SNS topic — it has no knowledge of downstream consumers. Adding a new workflow requires only creating a new SQS queue and subscribing it to the topic, with zero changes to the publishing service.
wrong_explanation_1: Directly invoking downstream Lambda functions creates tight coupling — the publishing service must know about every downstream workflow and must be updated every time a new one is added. This violates the extensibility requirement.
wrong_explanation_2: Polling a shared DynamoDB table creates contention between workflows and requires each workflow to implement its own polling logic, deduplication, and state tracking. It is operationally complex and does not scale well with many consumers.
wrong_explanation_3: A single Lambda function calling workflows in sequence creates a synchronous chain where a failure or slowness in one workflow blocks all subsequent ones. It also requires modifying the Lambda function to add new workflows, reintroducing the coupling problem.

scenario: A company wants to implement automated model retraining triggered by data drift detection. When SageMaker Model Monitor detects that the distribution of inference inputs has shifted significantly from the training baseline, the team wants to automatically kick off a SageMaker Pipeline to retrain the model. Which integration pattern achieves this?
correct_answer: Configure Model Monitor to emit a CloudWatch alarm on drift detection, and use an EventBridge rule to trigger the SageMaker Pipeline when the alarm fires
wrong_answer_1: Configure Model Monitor to directly invoke the SageMaker Pipeline via a built-in trigger
wrong_answer_2: Use AWS Lambda to poll Model Monitor results every hour and trigger the pipeline if drift is detected
wrong_answer_3: Use Amazon SNS to send a notification to the team, who then manually triggers the pipeline
correct_explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor publishes monitoring results as CloudWatch metrics. You can create a CloudWatch alarm that fires when drift exceeds a threshold, and an EventBridge rule can route that alarm event to trigger a SageMaker Pipeline execution. This is the standard event-driven pattern for automated retraining on drift detection.
wrong_explanation_1: SageMaker Model Monitor does not have a built-in direct trigger to invoke SageMaker Pipelines. The integration requires routing through CloudWatch alarms and EventBridge.
wrong_explanation_2: Polling Model Monitor results with Lambda every hour introduces unnecessary latency and complexity. The event-driven CloudWatch alarm + EventBridge pattern reacts immediately when drift is detected without polling.
wrong_explanation_3: Sending an SNS notification for manual pipeline triggering introduces human latency into what should be an automated retraining workflow. The goal is automated retraining, not human-in-the-loop notification.

scenario: A security team wants to require all IAM users in the account to provide a one-time code from a virtual authenticator app in addition to their password when signing in. Which capability should be enabled?
correct_answer: Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
wrong_answer_1: IAM Access Analyzer
wrong_answer_2: AWS Single Sign-On password rotation
wrong_answer_3: Service control policies (SCPs)
correct_explanation: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) requires a second factor — typically a one-time code from a virtual or hardware authenticator — in addition to a password. MFA can be enabled per IAM user and is required by best practice for the root user and privileged users.
wrong_explanation_1: IAM Access Analyzer identifies resources shared outside an account or organization. It does not affect sign-in flow.
wrong_explanation_2: Password rotation does not require a second factor. It only enforces periodic password changes, which is a weaker control than MFA.
wrong_explanation_3: SCPs limit what permissions IAM principals in an Organization can use. They do not control sign-in authentication factors.

scenario: A data engineering team runs an AWS Glue PySpark job that reads partitioned Parquet data from Amazon S3 and writes results back to S3. The job processes 2 TB of data daily and is consistently slow. Profiling shows that 90% of the processing time is spent on a shuffle operation caused by a join between a 2 TB fact table and a 500 MB dimension table. Which optimization should the team apply?
correct_answer: Use a broadcast join to distribute the smaller dimension table to all executors
wrong_answer_1: Increase the number of Glue DPUs allocated to the job
wrong_answer_2: Enable Glue job bookmarks to skip previously processed partitions
wrong_answer_3: Repartition the fact table to match the number of available executors
correct_explanation: When joining a large table with a small table (500 MB fits in executor memory), a broadcast join eliminates the shuffle entirely by sending a copy of the small table to every executor. This is the most effective optimization for this specific bottleneck and can reduce join time by orders of magnitude.
wrong_explanation_1: Adding more DPUs increases parallelism but does not eliminate the shuffle. The shuffle will still occur across all executors, just with more resources — the root cause of the slowness is not addressed.
wrong_explanation_2: Glue job bookmarks skip previously processed data to avoid reprocessing. They do not affect the performance of the join operation within a single job run.
wrong_explanation_3: Repartitioning the fact table changes how data is distributed across executors but does not eliminate the shuffle caused by the join. The shuffle will still occur when matching keys across partitions.

scenario: A data engineer needs to write a script that reads thousands of items from an Amazon DynamoDB table using a filter expression. The engineer notices that the script is making many API calls and consuming excessive read capacity. Which DynamoDB API operation and pattern should be used to efficiently retrieve all matching items?
correct_answer: Use the Scan operation with pagination via the LastEvaluatedKey
wrong_answer_1: Use the GetItem operation in a loop for each item
wrong_answer_2: Use the Query operation without a partition key
wrong_answer_3: Use the BatchWriteItem operation to retrieve items in bulk
correct_explanation: The DynamoDB Scan operation reads all items in a table and applies filter expressions. For large tables, Scan returns up to 1 MB of data per call. Using the LastEvaluatedKey from each response as the ExclusiveStartKey in the next call paginates through the entire table efficiently.
wrong_explanation_1: Using GetItem in a loop makes one API call per item, which is extremely inefficient for thousands of items. It consumes one read capacity unit per item and generates excessive API call overhead.
wrong_explanation_2: The DynamoDB Query operation requires a partition key value — it cannot be used without specifying a partition key. Without a partition key, Query is not a valid operation.
wrong_explanation_3: BatchWriteItem is used to write (put or delete) multiple items in a single request. It is a write operation and cannot be used to retrieve items from a table.

scenario: A team places an Amazon SQS queue between a producer service and a consumer service so that the producer can keep submitting work even when the consumer is being deployed. Which Well-Architected design principle does this illustrate?
correct_answer: Loose coupling using a queue
wrong_answer_1: Vertical scaling of monolithic services
wrong_answer_2: Centralizing authorization at the API gateway
wrong_answer_3: Co-locating producer and consumer on the same EC2 host
correct_explanation: Inserting a queue between producer and consumer is a textbook loose-coupling pattern. Producers and consumers can be deployed, scaled, and operated independently because they communicate asynchronously through SQS rather than via direct synchronous calls.
wrong_explanation_1: Vertical scaling addresses sizing of a single resource, not coupling between services.
wrong_explanation_2: Centralizing authorization is a separate concern; it does not address coupling between producer and consumer at deploy time.
wrong_explanation_3: Co-locating producer and consumer increases coupling and shared blast radius — the opposite of the principle.

scenario: A developer is building a Node.js application that runs on an on-premises Linux server and needs to call AWS services such as S3 and DynamoDB using the AWS SDK. The server is not an EC2 instance and cannot be assigned an IAM role. What is the MOST suitable way to provide AWS credentials to the application?
correct_answer: Create an IAM user with programmatic access and store the access keys in the credentials file at ~/.aws/credentials on the server.
wrong_answer_1: Assign an IAM role to the on-premises server and use the AssumeRole API to retrieve temporary credentials.
wrong_answer_2: Hardcode the AWS access keys directly in the application source code.
wrong_answer_3: Use the root account access keys stored in the credentials file.
correct_explanation: For applications running outside of AWS, access keys are the standard mechanism for programmatic access. The AWS SDK automatically reads credentials from the ~/.aws/credentials file on Linux servers. Creating a dedicated IAM user with only the required permissions and storing its access keys in the credentials file is the correct approach for on-premises SDK usage.
wrong_explanation_1: IAM roles can be assigned to EC2 instances, ECS tasks, and Lambda functions — not to arbitrary on-premises servers. While AWS Systems Manager hybrid activations can extend some IAM capabilities to on-premises servers, directly assigning a role to an on-premises server is not supported in the standard model.
wrong_explanation_2: Hardcoding access keys in source code is a critical security anti-pattern. Keys embedded in code are easily exposed through version control systems, code reviews, or accidental sharing. The credentials file keeps keys separate from the application code.
wrong_explanation_3: Root account access keys provide unrestricted access to all AWS resources and should never be created or used for application access. AWS strongly recommends against creating root access keys under any circumstances.

scenario: A data engineering team stores partitioned Parquet data in Amazon S3 and queries it using Amazon Athena. After adding new partitions to S3, queries do not return data from the new partitions. The team wants to automatically update the Glue Data Catalog with new partition metadata whenever partitions are added. Which approach automates partition discovery?
correct_answer: Run an AWS Glue crawler on a schedule to discover and add new partitions
wrong_answer_1: Run 'MSCK REPAIR TABLE' in Athena after each partition is added
wrong_answer_2: Manually run 'ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION' for each new partition
wrong_answer_3: Enable S3 Event Notifications to update the Glue Data Catalog
correct_explanation: AWS Glue crawlers can run on a schedule to automatically discover new partitions in S3 and update the Glue Data Catalog. This eliminates the need for manual intervention and ensures that Athena queries always have access to the latest partitions.
wrong_explanation_1: Running 'MSCK REPAIR TABLE' in Athena can add new partitions, but it requires manual execution after each partition is added. This does not automate partition discovery and requires ongoing manual intervention.
wrong_explanation_2: Manually running 'ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION' for each new partition is time-consuming and error-prone. It does not automate partition discovery and does not scale well as the number of partitions grows.
wrong_explanation_3: S3 Event Notifications can trigger Lambda functions in response to object creation events, but they do not natively update the Glue Data Catalog. You would need to write custom Lambda code to add partitions, which is more complex than using a scheduled Glue crawler.

scenario: A machine learning team is building a SageMaker training pipeline that requires a custom preprocessing step using a library not available in any SageMaker managed container. The team wants to run this step as a SageMaker Processing job. What is the correct approach to provide the custom environment?
correct_answer: Build a custom Docker image with the required library, push it to Amazon ECR, and specify it as the image URI in the SageMaker Processing job configuration
wrong_answer_1: Use a SageMaker notebook instance to run the preprocessing step before submitting the training job
wrong_answer_2: Install the library using pip in the processing script's entry point before importing it
wrong_answer_3: Use AWS Lambda to run the preprocessing step with the custom library installed as a Lambda layer
correct_explanation: SageMaker Processing jobs support custom Docker containers. You build an image with the required library, push it to ECR, and reference the ECR image URI in the ProcessingJob configuration. This is the standard BYOC pattern for SageMaker Processing jobs with custom dependencies.
wrong_explanation_1: Running preprocessing in a notebook instance is not a scalable or reproducible approach for a production pipeline. Notebook instances are interactive environments, not managed processing job infrastructure.
wrong_explanation_2: Installing packages via pip at runtime in the processing script's entry point is unreliable in isolated container environments and may fail due to network restrictions or missing build tools. Dependencies should be baked into the Docker image at build time.
wrong_explanation_3: AWS Lambda has a 15-minute execution limit, a 10 GB memory cap, and is not designed for data-intensive ML preprocessing workloads. SageMaker Processing jobs provide managed, scalable compute specifically designed for ML preprocessing.

scenario: A developer is working on a DynamoDB table that stores item-level changes. When an item is updated, the developer needs a Lambda function to receive only the item's state before the modification — not the new value — so it can be archived to S3. Which DynamoDB Streams StreamViewType should the developer configure?
correct_answer: OLD_IMAGE
wrong_answer_1: NEW_IMAGE
wrong_answer_2: KEYS_ONLY
wrong_answer_3: NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES
correct_explanation: OLD_IMAGE writes the entire item as it appeared before the modification to the stream. This gives the Lambda function access to the pre-update state of the item, which can then be archived to S3. It is the correct StreamViewType when only the previous value is needed.
wrong_explanation_1: NEW_IMAGE writes the entire item as it appears after the modification. This provides the post-update state, not the pre-update state that the developer needs to archive.
wrong_explanation_2: KEYS_ONLY writes only the key attributes of the modified item to the stream. It does not include any attribute values, making it impossible to archive the full previous state of the item.
wrong_explanation_3: NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES writes both the pre-update and post-update states of the item to the stream. While this includes the old image, it also sends the new image, which is unnecessary overhead. The developer only needs the old image, so OLD_IMAGE is the more precise and appropriate choice.

scenario: A development team wants to run Docker containers without managing the underlying EC2 instances. They want AWS to provision compute on demand for each task. Which combination of services meets this requirement?
correct_answer: Amazon ECS with the AWS Fargate launch type
wrong_answer_1: Amazon ECS with the EC2 launch type
wrong_answer_2: Amazon EC2 with Docker installed manually
wrong_answer_3: Amazon EMR with custom containers
correct_explanation: AWS Fargate is the serverless compute engine for containers. Using Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type lets the team run containers without provisioning or managing EC2 instances — AWS provisions and scales compute per task.
wrong_explanation_1: ECS with the EC2 launch type requires the customer to manage the underlying EC2 cluster, defeating the goal of avoiding server management.
wrong_explanation_2: Running Docker on EC2 manually means managing instances, patching, and scaling — the opposite of serverless container compute.
wrong_explanation_3: EMR is a big-data processing service for frameworks like Spark and Hadoop. It is not the standard service for general-purpose container workloads.

scenario: A machine learning team is preparing a training dataset for a classification model. After profiling the data, they discover that one feature has a very high correlation (r = 0.98) with another feature already in the dataset. Including both features may cause multicollinearity issues. Which approach should the team take?
correct_answer: Remove one of the two highly correlated features from the dataset
wrong_answer_1: Apply SMOTE to both features to reduce their correlation
wrong_answer_2: Apply one-hot encoding to both features
wrong_answer_3: Impute both features with their respective means
correct_explanation: When two features are highly correlated (r = 0.98), they carry nearly identical information. Keeping both can cause multicollinearity in linear models, inflate feature importance scores, and add noise without adding predictive value. Removing one of the redundant features simplifies the model and reduces the risk of these issues.
wrong_explanation_1: SMOTE is an oversampling technique for addressing class imbalance in the target variable. It generates synthetic samples and does not reduce or modify the correlation between input features.
wrong_explanation_2: One-hot encoding is used for categorical features. Applying it to numeric features would destroy their continuous information and is not applicable to addressing multicollinearity between numeric columns.
wrong_explanation_3: Imputing with the mean fills in missing values and does not change the correlation structure between features. It does not address multicollinearity between two fully observed, highly correlated features.

scenario: A developer has several API Gateway REST APIs, each corresponding to a different release stage of an application: ALPHA, BETA, and PROD. The company wants to consolidate these into a single API Gateway deployment where each stage points to a different Lambda function version. Clients connect using stage-specific custom domain names. What is the MOST suitable approach to achieve this?
correct_answer: Use API Gateway stage variables to reference different Lambda function ARNs per stage.
wrong_answer_1: Create separate API Gateway deployments for each stage and use Route 53 to route traffic.
wrong_answer_2: Use Lambda aliases to point to different function versions and configure a single API Gateway stage.
wrong_answer_3: Use API Gateway usage plans to assign different Lambda functions to different API keys.
correct_explanation: Stage variables in API Gateway are key-value pairs that can be defined per stage and referenced in integration URIs. By setting a stage variable (e.g., lambdaAlias) to different values in each stage, a single API Gateway can route requests to different Lambda function versions or aliases without changing the API definition. This is the standard pattern for managing multiple release environments in a single API Gateway.
wrong_explanation_1: Creating separate API Gateway deployments per stage defeats the purpose of consolidation. The requirement is a single API Gateway with multiple stages, not multiple separate deployments.
wrong_explanation_2: Lambda aliases alone do not solve the problem of routing different stages to different function versions within a single API Gateway. Stage variables are needed to dynamically reference the correct alias or ARN per stage.
wrong_explanation_3: Usage plans and API keys control throttling and quota limits for API consumers. They are not a mechanism for routing requests to different Lambda function versions based on the deployment stage.

scenario: A security team wants to prevent any IAM principal in member accounts of an AWS Organization from using the EC2 instance launch API in a specific Region, regardless of what permissions are granted at the account level. Which feature should the team use?
correct_answer: Service control policies (SCPs)
wrong_answer_1: IAM identity-based policies
wrong_answer_2: Resource-based policies
wrong_answer_3: Permissions boundaries on individual users
correct_explanation: Service control policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations define the maximum permissions available to IAM principals in member accounts. An SCP that denies the EC2 launch action in a Region is enforced regardless of identity-based grants in those accounts.
wrong_explanation_1: IAM identity-based policies grant permissions. They can be bypassed via account-level configuration changes if no account-wide guardrail exists.
wrong_explanation_2: Resource-based policies attach to specific resources and control access to those resources. They do not impose an organization-wide cap on launching EC2.
wrong_explanation_3: Permissions boundaries cap the permissions of an individual user or role within a single account. They do not provide an organization-wide guardrail across all accounts.

scenario: Which IAM principle states that a user, role, or service should be granted only the permissions necessary to complete its assigned tasks — and nothing more?
correct_answer: Principle of least privilege
wrong_answer_1: Principle of shared responsibility
wrong_answer_2: Principle of separation of duties
wrong_answer_3: Principle of defense in depth
correct_explanation: The principle of least privilege grants only the minimum permissions required to perform a task. Following this principle reduces blast radius if a credential is compromised and is a fundamental IAM best practice.
wrong_explanation_1: Shared responsibility describes the division of security duties between AWS and customers. It is not specifically about permission scoping.
wrong_explanation_2: Separation of duties divides sensitive tasks across multiple people to prevent fraud. It is related but distinct from least privilege.
wrong_explanation_3: Defense in depth is layered security across the stack (network, host, application). It is a security strategy, not a permission-granting principle.

scenario: An enterprise wants billing experts who help with account-level billing investigation, payment methods, and consolidated billing complications, included as part of their AWS Support plan. Which AWS Support tier includes this Concierge billing support?
correct_answer: AWS Enterprise Support
wrong_answer_1: AWS Basic Support
wrong_answer_2: AWS Developer Support
wrong_answer_3: AWS Business Support
correct_explanation: The Concierge Support team — a billing and account specialist team — is exclusive to AWS Enterprise Support. They assist with billing analysis, payment, and account-management questions for enterprise customers.
wrong_explanation_1: Basic Support does not include Concierge billing support.
wrong_explanation_2: Developer Support is a lower paid tier and does not include Concierge.
wrong_explanation_3: Business Support adds 24/7 Cloud Support Engineer access but does not include the Concierge team.

scenario: A platform team allows application developers to create their own IAM roles for Lambda functions but wants to ensure that the roles can never grant permissions outside an approved set (for example, no S3 wildcard access). Which IAM feature limits the maximum permissions that any role a developer creates can have?
correct_answer: IAM permissions boundary
wrong_answer_1: Resource-based policy on each S3 bucket
wrong_answer_2: IAM access key rotation
wrong_answer_3: Identity-based policy attached to the developer
correct_explanation: Permissions boundaries set the maximum permissions a principal can have, regardless of the identity-based policies attached. Requiring developers to attach a specific boundary to roles they create enforces an upper limit on those roles' capabilities.
wrong_explanation_1: Per-bucket resource policies control access to specific resources but do not cap what permissions a created role can be granted across the account.
wrong_explanation_2: Access-key rotation addresses credential hygiene; it does not bound permissions.
wrong_explanation_3: An identity-based policy on the developer grants their permissions but does not cap what roles they may create.

scenario: A data engineering team wants to automate the execution of an AWS Glue ETL job every day at 2 AM UTC to process the previous day's data. The job should not run on weekends. Which approach should they use to schedule this job?
correct_answer: Create an AWS Glue scheduled trigger with a cron expression
wrong_answer_1: Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler with a rate expression
wrong_answer_2: Configure an AWS Lambda function to start the Glue job using a CloudWatch Events rule
wrong_answer_3: Use AWS Step Functions with a Wait state to delay execution until 2 AM
correct_explanation: AWS Glue supports scheduled triggers with cron expressions that can specify exact times and days of the week. A cron expression like cron(0 2 ? * MON-FRI *) runs the job at 2 AM UTC on weekdays only, directly within the Glue console without additional services.
wrong_explanation_1: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler with a rate expression runs at a fixed interval from the last execution and cannot exclude specific days of the week. A cron-based schedule is needed to exclude weekends.
wrong_explanation_2: Using Lambda with a CloudWatch Events rule adds unnecessary complexity. AWS Glue natively supports scheduled triggers with cron expressions, making a Lambda intermediary redundant for this use case.
wrong_explanation_3: AWS Step Functions Wait states pause a workflow execution for a specified duration or until a timestamp. They are not a scheduling mechanism and cannot trigger a job on a recurring daily schedule.

scenario: An operations team wants to execute a command — such as installing a patch or restarting a service — across hundreds of EC2 instances simultaneously, without SSH'ing into each one. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
correct_answer: AWS Systems Manager Run Command
wrong_answer_1: AWS CodeDeploy
wrong_answer_2: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
wrong_answer_3: AWS OpsWorks
correct_explanation: AWS Systems Manager Run Command lets operators execute commands or scripts across many managed instances at once, with audit logging and IAM-based authorization. SSH access is not required because the SSM agent on each instance receives the command.
wrong_explanation_1: CodeDeploy automates application deployments. It is not a general-purpose ad-hoc command runner.
wrong_explanation_2: EC2 Auto Scaling adjusts the size of a fleet. It does not execute commands on existing instances.
wrong_explanation_3: OpsWorks is a configuration management service based on Chef and Puppet. It is heavier and not the standard tool for ad-hoc command execution today.

scenario: A company is migrating a database containing personally identifiable information (PII) to Amazon RDS. The security team requires that the data be encrypted at rest and that the encryption key be rotated annually. The team also needs to ensure that if the RDS instance is deleted, the final snapshot is also encrypted. Which approach should the solutions architect take?
correct_answer: Enable RDS encryption at rest using a customer managed KMS key when creating the instance, and enable automatic key rotation on the CMK. Encrypted instances automatically produce encrypted snapshots.
wrong_answer_1: Enable RDS encryption after the instance is created by modifying the instance settings in the console.
wrong_answer_2: Use Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) within the database engine and store the TDE certificate in AWS Certificate Manager.
wrong_answer_3: Encrypt the data at the application layer before writing to RDS and store the encryption keys in AWS Secrets Manager.
correct_explanation: RDS encryption at rest must be enabled at instance creation time and uses AWS KMS. When a customer managed key is used, automatic rotation can be enabled on the CMK. All snapshots of an encrypted RDS instance, including the final snapshot on deletion, are automatically encrypted with the same key — satisfying all requirements.
wrong_explanation_1: RDS encryption cannot be enabled on an existing unencrypted instance by modifying it in place. To encrypt an unencrypted RDS instance, you must take a snapshot, copy it with encryption enabled, and restore from the encrypted snapshot.
wrong_explanation_2: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) is supported for Oracle and SQL Server on RDS, but AWS Certificate Manager is for SSL/TLS certificates, not TDE certificates. TDE certificates for RDS are managed differently and this approach does not integrate with KMS for key rotation.
wrong_explanation_3: Application-layer encryption is a valid defense-in-depth measure but does not satisfy the requirement for encryption at rest at the storage level. It also adds significant application complexity and does not ensure that snapshots are encrypted at the RDS level.

scenario: A data engineering team needs to grant an AWS Glue ETL job access to read from an Amazon S3 bucket and write to an Amazon Redshift cluster. Following the principle of least privilege, which approach should be used?
correct_answer: Create an IAM role with specific S3 read and Redshift write permissions and attach it as the Glue job's IAM role
wrong_answer_1: Use the AWS root account credentials in the Glue job configuration
wrong_answer_2: Create an IAM user with AdministratorAccess and pass the access keys as Glue job parameters
wrong_answer_3: Grant the Glue job s3:* and redshift:* permissions on all resources
correct_explanation: IAM roles are the correct mechanism for granting AWS service access to other AWS services. Creating a role with only the specific permissions needed (s3:GetObject on the source bucket, redshift:CopyFromS3 on the target cluster) follows least privilege and avoids exposing long-lived credentials.
wrong_explanation_1: Using root account credentials violates AWS security best practices. Root credentials have unrestricted access to all AWS resources and should never be used for programmatic service access.
wrong_explanation_2: Creating an IAM user with AdministratorAccess and passing access keys as job parameters violates least privilege and exposes long-lived credentials in the job configuration. IAM roles are the correct mechanism for service-to-service access.
wrong_explanation_3: Granting s3:* and redshift:* on all resources gives the Glue job far more access than needed. If the job were compromised, an attacker could access or modify any S3 bucket or Redshift cluster in the account.

scenario: A data engineering team stores large Parquet datasets in Amazon S3. Over time, many small files (under 128 KB each) have accumulated due to frequent incremental writes. Queries using Amazon Athena are slow because of the overhead of opening thousands of small files. Which approach improves query performance by reducing the number of files?
correct_answer: Use an AWS Glue ETL job to compact small files into larger files
wrong_answer_1: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration to speed up file access
wrong_answer_2: Use S3 Select to filter data before reading files
wrong_answer_3: Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering to optimize storage costs
correct_explanation: AWS Glue ETL jobs can read multiple small Parquet files from S3, combine them into larger files (e.g., 128 MB or larger), and write the compacted files back to S3. This reduces the number of files Athena must open, significantly improving query performance. This process is called file compaction or coalescing.
wrong_explanation_1: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads and downloads to S3 by routing through CloudFront edge locations. It does not reduce the number of files or improve query performance for Athena, which is bottlenecked by the overhead of opening many small files.
wrong_explanation_2: S3 Select allows you to retrieve a subset of data from an object using SQL expressions, reducing the amount of data transferred. However, it does not reduce the number of files or the overhead of opening thousands of small files.
wrong_explanation_3: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers to optimize storage costs. It does not compact small files or improve query performance.

scenario: In a supervised learning dataset for predicting house prices, the columns are square footage, number of bedrooms, year built, and final sale price. Which column is the TARGET variable, and which are FEATURES?
correct_answer: Final sale price is the target; square footage, bedrooms, and year built are features
wrong_answer_1: Square footage is the target; the rest are features
wrong_answer_2: Number of bedrooms is the target; the rest are features
wrong_answer_3: Year built is the target; the rest are features
